about.title: Cypress Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products show up everywhere in daily life around Cypress — a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a car part that fails on Valley View Street, a power tool used in a garage near Walker Street, or a piece of furniture that tips over at home. California treats many of these cases under strict liability, meaning the person hurt generally doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused the injury. That's a meaningful difference from other injury claims, and it can shape who gets pursued: the maker, the distributor, or the retailer that sold the item. If a defective product hurt you or a family member in Cypress, keeping the item itself matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can look at what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Cypress Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Path Forward
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused harm. An attorney can help identify which theory (design, manufacturing, or warning defect) fits your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California product liability law. That matters in a city like Cypress where products purchased locally may have been made and distributed far outside Orange County.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Since these cases often hinge on examining the defective item itself, keeping it safe and unaltered is critical. An attorney can advise on how to properly preserve evidence before it's lost, discarded, or repaired.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims frequently rely on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury, rather than on the manufacturer's conduct. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain which legal theory may apply.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, if it's safe to store. Don't repair, modify, or discard it, since the physical product is often central evidence in these claims. Photograph packaging, receipts, and any warning labels if you have them.

items.question: I live near Valley View Street in Cypress — does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't determine liability, but it can help establish the timeline and circumstances of your injury, especially if the incident involved a vehicle part or roadside equipment. An attorney connected through LawProactive can walk through the specific details of what happened near you.

items.question: Is there really no cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and there's no charge to be matched with an independent attorney. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
